verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the holy gifts that the people of Israel set apart for me, so that they do not dishonour my holy name. I am the LORD.

Tell them: For all time to come, if any of your descendants is unclean and comes near the holy gifts that the people of Israel set apart for the LORD, that person must be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.

None of Aaron's descendants who has a serious skin disease or a flow from his body may eat the holy gifts until he is clean. Anyone who touches something made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has a release of seed,
or anyone who touches a crawling creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean in any way,
will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy gifts unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down, he will be clean. After that he may eat the holy gifts, because they are his food.
He must not eat an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals, because it would make him unclean. I am the LORD.
The priests must keep my commands, or they will become guilty and die for dishonouring them. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
No one outside a priest's family may eat the holy gifts. A guest staying with a priest, or a hired worker, must not eat them.
But if a priest buys a slave with his money, the slave may eat them, and so may slaves born in his house. They may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries someone who is not a priest, she may no longer eat the special gifts from the holy offerings.

But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, and has no children, and comes back to live in her father's house as when she was young, she may eat her father's food. But no one outside the family may eat any of it.
If someone eats a holy gift by mistake, he must give the priest the same amount of holy food, plus one fifth more.
The priests must not dishonour the holy gifts that the people of Israel offer to the LORD
by letting the people eat them, which would bring guilt on them. For I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel, and tell them: Any Israelite, or any foreigner in Israel, may bring a burnt offering to the LORD, either to keep a promise or as a gift freely given.
To be accepted for you, it must be a male bull, sheep, or goat with nothing wrong with it.
Do not offer anything that has something wrong with it, because it will not be accepted for you.
When anyone brings a peace offering to the LORD from the cattle or the flock, to keep a promise or as a freely given gift, it must be perfect to be accepted. There must be nothing wrong with it.
Do not offer the LORD an animal that is blind, injured, or crippled, or that has warts, sores, or a running skin disease. Do not put any of these on the altar as a gift made by fire to the LORD.
You may offer a bull or a lamb that has a body part too long or too short as a freely given gift, but it will not be accepted to keep a promise.
Do not offer the LORD an animal whose private parts are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. Do not do this in your land.
Do not accept animals like these from a foreigner and offer them as the food of your God. They are damaged and have something wrong with them, so they will not be accepted for you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"When a calf, a lamb, or a young goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Do not kill a cow or a sheep on the same day as its young.
When you offer a thank offering to the LORD, offer it in the right way so that it will be accepted for you.
It must be eaten on the same day. Leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep my commands and obey them. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonour my holy name. I must be honoured as holy among the people of Israel. I am the LORD, who makes you holy,
who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
